summary: The candidate quickly diagnosed the actual root cause — the sweep releasing original rather than remaining unit counts — stated it explicitly before editing, applied a direct fix, and confirmed the test suite passed. The session was efficient and accurate but light on narration during implementation and lacked any closing reflection tying the fix back to the mechanism.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate read the failing test and immediately identified the discrepancy in expected vs actual units without needing to ask clarifying questions, and the test itself was self-explanatory. There was no genuine ambiguity left to resolve here — the test body made the expected behavior clear, so no clarifying question was necessary or observed.

Before touching code, the candidate explicitly named the mechanism: the sweep releases the original unit count instead of the remaining count. This is precisely the root cause and specific enough to be wrong, meeting the bar cleanly.

The candidate narrated the key diagnostic moment (the diff showing shipped units returning) and stated the hypothesis before editing, giving an interviewer a thread to follow. However, narration was sparse — nothing was said during the actual edit or around the verification step, so the transcript alone leaves gaps in the reasoning trail.

The edit to src/sweep.ts was made immediately following the stated hypothesis and was saved promptly, showing a direct, coherent translation of the plan into code with no scattered or contradictory changes observed.

The candidate re-ran the test suite after the fix and confirmed a pass before ending the session, which is the core verification behavior expected. There is no evidence they checked edge cases beyond the single failing test (e.g., confirming full-release holds still behave correctly), so it's a basic but sufficient verification rather than a thorough one.

After the tests passed, the candidate ended the session immediately without any closing statement connecting the fix back to the root cause or explaining why releasing remaining units (versus original) resolves the phantom stock issue. Despite having correctly diagnosed the mechanism earlier, no reflective wrap-up was given at the point of resolution.
